title: ci(registry): test-suite-registry omits pkarr deploy-probe/deploy-verification and cold-store bounded-decompress — and its pkarr "broken clean checkout" reason is stale (suite now passes 61/61 via npm ci)

body:
## Problem

`.github/test-suite-registry.json` under-reports two suites it already carries an entry for, and the pkarr entry's stated blocker is no longer true on main — so triage reading the registry gets both the coverage count and the reason wrong.

### 1. pkarr-worker entry: 2 of 4 test files missing; reason stale

Registry entry `pkarr-worker` lists only:

- `pkgs/pkarr-worker/test/deploy-args.test.ts`
- `pkgs/pkarr-worker/test/worker.test.ts`

and gives the reason: "Clean-checkout execution is broken by lockfile mismatch and Vitest/pool-workers incompatibility; make runnable before wiring."

On current main (`aa01b61853`) the package has four test files, and the suite runs clean from a pristine extract:

- `test/worker.test.ts` — 36 tests
- `test/deploy-args.test.ts` — 13 tests
- `test/deploy-probe.test.ts` — 7 tests (**not in registry**; pins the #4865 existence-probe fix)
- `test/deploy-verification.test.ts` — 5 tests (**not in registry**; pins the #6476 post-deploy health verification)

Verified this run on the laptop (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-pkarr-20261108`, `git archive origin/main` extract): `package.json` requires `vitest ^3.2.7` and `package-lock.json` pins vitest 3.2.7 (in sync); `npm ci` succeeds and `npm test` reports **Test Files 4 passed, Tests 61 passed**. The lockfile/vitest-4 breakage described in #6093 and repeated in the registry reason has been fixed on main; what remains of #6093 is only the no-workflow wiring gap, not a broken suite.

### 2. cold-store-reaper.worker entry: the #6590 regression suite is missing

Registry entry `cold-store-reaper.worker` lists `test/run-local-proof.mjs` and `test/range-ignored.test.mjs` but omits `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/worker/test/bounded-decompress.test.mjs` — the regression suite for #6590 (zstd decompression bounded by the manifest's expected plaintext size; a hostile bundle member expanding past the Worker memory limit instead of a clean 502). The file is wired into the package's own `npm test` (`package.json` test script runs all three files). Verified this run on the laptop (probe `~/git/fleet/probe-coldstore-20261108`): `node test/bounded-decompress.test.mjs` passes, ending `PASS: bounded decompression (issue #6590)`.

## Why it matters

The registry is the inventory the coverage work (#6185 family, ratchet #6188) and every creator/sweep lane reads to decide what is verified and what is blocked. An entry that omits a third of a suite's files and states a fixed breakage as the current blocker sends fixers to re-diagnose a solved problem and undercounts the tests that would be wired by #6093 / the cold-store venue work.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `pkarr-worker` registry entry lists all four test files under `pkgs/pkarr-worker/test/` (worker, deploy-args, deploy-probe, deploy-verification).
- [ ] The pkarr entry's reason no longer claims a lockfile/runner breakage; it states the current verified state (suite runnable via `npm ci && npm test`, 61 tests passing at the verifying commit) and that the remaining gap is venue wiring (#6093).
- [ ] `cold-store-reaper.worker` registry entry lists `pkgs/cold-store-reaper/worker/test/bounded-decompress.test.mjs`.
- [ ] Registry `uncovered_count` / audit metadata are left consistent with the edited entries (no count change is expected: both suites' venue status is unchanged — this is a paths/reason correction, not a wiring change).

Related: #6093 (pkarr venue wiring — its breakage premise should also be re-checked against this evidence), #6188 (coverage ratchet), #6590, #4865, #6476.
